items.title: The declared driven model: prescribed time-dependent energy families, propagator evolution and the two-level drive models
items.statement:
## Definition

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) for a declared system, in the state, sharp-observable and evolution readings of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]; units are those of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The readings below are the reading of clause (iv) of P4 for the page's models; clause (iv) records that a prescribed time-dependent family is **a different model assumption** from the autonomous one, and clause (b) below adopts it.

**(b) Prescribed energy family.** As an additional model assumption of the pair, fix a nonempty compact interval $I=[a,b]\subset\mathbb R$ of physical times (seconds), the declared state space $\mathfrak H$ of the system, a value $\hbar>0$ of the reduced Planck constant as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and a **prescribed family** $t\mapsto H(t)$ of self-adjoint operators on $\mathfrak H$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]) in one of the following three **regularity classes**, whose hypotheses are part of the model declaration:

- **(i) Bounded norm-continuous class.** $D(H(t))=\mathfrak H$ for every $t$; each $H(t)\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is self-adjoint ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]); $t\mapsto H(t)$ is norm-continuous on $I$ ([[def-operator-norm]]); and $K:=\sup_{t\in I}\|H(t)\|/\hbar<\infty$.
- **(ii) Bounded-control class.** $H(t)=H_{0}+V(t)$, where $H_{0}$ is self-adjoint with domain $D(H_{0})\subseteq\mathfrak H$ and $V:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is strongly continuous with self-adjoint values and $\|V(t)\|=v(t)$, $v:=\sup_{t\in I}v(t)<\infty$.
- **(iii) Common-domain class.** There is a dense linear subspace $Y\subseteq\mathfrak H$ that is itself a Hilbert space continuously embedded in $\mathfrak H$ ([[def-hilbert-space]], for instance $Y=D(H_{0})$ with the graph norm of a self-adjoint $H_{0}$), with $D(H(t))=Y$ for every $t$, each $H(t)$ self-adjoint as an operator on $\mathfrak H$, and $t\mapsto H(t)$ of class $C^{1}(I;\mathcal B(Y,\mathfrak H))$.

The family, its class and its data are **prescribed**: no field equation, source model, back-reaction or feedback of the system on the source is assumed, and no claim is made that any laboratory arrangement realizes the family. The family is coupled to the system through the material hypotheses of the page or of the item that declares a specific model (for instance a magnetic-moment or electric-dipole coupling, or the external-source Coulomb family of the page's adiabatic models); the reading of $H(t)$ as the energy of the declared system is a model assumption.

**(c) The model's evolution.** The **driven model** declares that the time evolution of the system between times $s,t\in I$ is carried by a family $U(t,s)$ of unitary operators on $\mathfrak H$ with
$$U(s,s)=I,\qquad U(t,r)=U(t,s)U(s,r)\quad(r,s,t\in I),\qquad U(t,s)^{*}=U(s,t),$$
jointly strongly continuous in $(t,s)$, solving the time-dependent Schroedinger equation on $I$ in the sense of the class:
in class (i) $U$ is the unique norm-continuous solution of $i\hbar\partial_tU(t,s)=H(t)U(t,s)$ with $U(s,s)=I$ constructed by the Dyson series of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-norm-dyson-series-and-uniqueness]] (whose hypothesis is exactly the norm-continuity of the bounded self-adjoint family);
in class (ii) $U$ is the mild propagator constructed in [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-strong-bounded-interaction-picture]], satisfying $U(t,s)\psi=E(t-s)\psi-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_s^tE(t-r)V(r)U(r,s)\psi\,dr$ for every $\psi\in\mathfrak H$, with $E(u)=e^{-iuH_{0}/\hbar}$ the autonomous flow of clause (b) of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]];
in class (iii) $U$ is the strong propagator of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-common-domain-nonautonomous-evolution]] with physical generator $A=H/\hbar$, preserving $Y$, for which $t\mapsto U(t,s)y$ is $C^1$ in $\mathfrak H$ with $i\hbar\partial_tU(t,s)y=H(t)U(t,s)y$ for every $y\in Y$.
In each class the cited item is what makes the declaration well posed: it constructs the family and proves uniqueness under the class hypotheses. The model asserts nothing beyond those hypotheses; in particular it asserts no invariant domain and no strong equation for $H_{0}$-domain vectors in class (ii), and no common domain in classes (i) and (ii).

**(d) State and outcome readings.** The **evolved preparation** at time $t$ of a preparation $\rho$ specified at time $s$ is $\rho(t):=U(t,s)\rho(s)U(t,s)^{*}$; it is a preparation of the model in the sense of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] for every $t$, by unitarity of $U(t,s)$ and [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]. A pure preparation $[\psi(s)]$ evolves to the pure preparation $[\psi(t)]$ with $\psi(t):=U(t,s)\psi(s)\ne0$. The **outcome law at time $t$** of an assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]) in that preparation is $\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}$, the reading of P2; the definition records the timing convention once and asserts nothing about how or when a record is produced.

**(e) Energy-basis amplitudes and level populations.** In class (ii), let $(\varphi_{j})_{j\in J}$ be an orthonormal family in $D(H_{0})$ with $H_{0}\varphi_{j}=E_{j}\varphi_{j}$ and $E_{j}\in\mathbb R$ (a complete orthonormal family of eigenvectors is not assumed here). For $s\le t$ and labels $i,j$ the **transition amplitude from $i$ at time $s$ to $j$ at time $t$** is the scalar
$$A_{ji}(t,s):=e^{iE_{j}(t-s)/\hbar}\,\bigl\langle U(t,s)\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\bigr\rangle ,$$
and the **transition probability** is $p_{ji}(t,s):=|A_{ji}(t,s)|^{2}$. If additionally $E_{j}$ is a simple eigenvalue of $H_{0}$ with spectral projection $P_{j}=E_{H_{0}}(\{E_{j}\})$ onto $\mathbb C\varphi_{j}$, then the definition *states*, as the reading of P2, the identity
$$p_{ji}(t,s)=\mu^{H_{0}}_{\psi(t)}(\{E_{j}\})=\|E_{H_{0}}(\{E_{j}\})\psi(t)\|^{2},\qquad \psi(t)=U(t,s)\varphi_{i},$$
which follows from the rank-one form of $P_{j}$ and the normalization $\|\varphi_{j}\|=1$; $p_{ji}$ is the reading of the outcome probability of the value $E_{j}$ of the assigned energy observable $(H_{0},\mathrm J)$ in the evolved preparation, and it is a property of the declared model, not a measured frequency.

**(f) Declared two-level drive models.** Let $(\sigma_{x},\sigma_{y},\sigma_{z})$ be the Pauli matrices of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e) acting on $\mathbb C^{2}$ in the orthonormal basis $(e_{\uparrow},e_{\downarrow})$ ([[def-inner-product-space]]), let $\omega_{0},\Omega_{1},\omega\in\mathbb R$, and put $H_{0}:=\frac{\hbar}{2}\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}$ (class (i) with $I$ any compact interval). The **circular two-level drive model** is the class-(i) family
$$H_{\mathrm c}(t):=\frac{\hbar}{2}\Bigl(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\bigl(\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{x}+\sin(\omega t)\sigma_{y}\bigr)\Bigr),$$
and the **linear two-level drive model** is the class-(i) family
$$H_{\mathrm l}(t):=\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{x}\bigr).$$
The dimensionless numbers $\omega_{0},\Omega_{1},\omega$ are read as angular frequencies in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$; $\omega_{0}$ is the **splitting frequency** of the model (the level gap is $\hbar|\omega_{0}|$), $\omega$ the **drive frequency**, $\Omega_{1}$ the **transverse coupling**, and $\Delta:=\omega_{0}-\omega$ the **detuning**. Populations of the level pair are the diagonal entries $\langle P_{\bullet}\psi,\psi\rangle$ of the orthogonal projections $P_{\uparrow},P_{\downarrow}$ onto $\mathbb Ce_{\uparrow},\mathbb Ce_{\downarrow}$ in the evolved vector $\psi(t)$. The two families are model data: no identification with a laboratory spin, molecule or field, and no relation of $\Omega_{1}$ to a field amplitude, is asserted; such an identification is a tested identification in the sense of P7.

**(g) Status and scope.** Clauses (b), (c), (f) are adopted model assumptions and readings; the existence and uniqueness of the propagator in each class is cited mathematics, not a consequence of P1, P2 or P4. The model asserts no open-system or environment coupling, no non-unitary reduced dynamics, no measurement or apparatus model, no thermalization or equilibration, no long-time limit and no empirical record; the identification of the family's parameters with laboratory fields and of the system with a laboratory sample is made, if at all, only in separately declared models with their own uncertainty.

## Remarks

- **Why classes (i)-(iii) instead of one general theorem.** A general unbounded time-dependent family requires a domain condition; classes (ii) and (iii) are the two standard sufficient regimes used on this page, and the bounded class (i) covers the finite-level models. Clause (iv) of P4 explicitly does not adopt a general unbounded family, so each class is declared with its own mathematics.
- **Amplitudes are not outcomes.** The scalar $A_{ji}$ is a complex bookkeeping amplitude; the model's outcome probability is the Born number of clause (e). Global phases of the eigenvectors change $A_{ji}$ by a phase and leave $p_{ji}$ unchanged.

items.physical_scope: The driven-dynamics model of a declared system of the framework: a prescribed time-dependent family of self-adjoint energy operators in one of three declared regularity classes (bounded norm-continuous on a compact interval; a fixed self-adjoint part plus a strongly continuous bounded self-adjoint control; a common-domain C^1 family), the unitary two-time propagator declared to carry the state evolution, the reading of preparations and outcome laws at the running time, the energy-basis transition amplitudes and level populations, and the two declared two-level drive models (circular and linear polarization). The definition fixes terminology and readings only: it adopts the driven-evolution assumption as an additional model assumption beyond P4, and asserts no existence theorem (supplied by the cited mathematics in each class), no laboratory realization, no measurement, no open system, no equilibration and no empirical result.

items.title: The interaction picture of the declared driven model: readings, the interaction propagator and picture equivalence of outcome laws
items.statement:
## Definition

**(a) Setting.** Adopt the framework data and the declared driven model of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] in the **bounded-control class** of its clause (b)(ii): $\mathfrak H$ is the model's state space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), $H_{0}$ is self-adjoint on its exact dense domain $D(H_{0})$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), $V:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is strongly continuous with self-adjoint values and $v=\sup_{t\in I}\|V(t)\|<\infty$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]), $H(t)=H_{0}+V(t)$ on $D(H_{0})$, and $U(t,s)$ is the mild propagator of clause (c)(ii) constructed in [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-strong-bounded-interaction-picture]]. The readings of P1 and P2 are those of [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] and [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]; all times lie in $I$ and are read in seconds as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) The free-flow factor.** The **free-flow factor** of the model is the autonomous flow of the unperturbed part,
$$E(t):=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the reading of clause (b) of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] applied to the assigned energy observable $(H_{0},\mathrm J)$; it is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group on all real arguments. This auxiliary group supplies $E(-t)$ and $E(t-s)$ even when those arguments lie outside $I$; the physical driven evaluation times $s,t$ remain in $I$. The **interaction-picture control** is the family $V_{I}:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$,
$$V_{I}(t):=E(-t)V(t)E(t),$$
which is strongly continuous with self-adjoint values and $\|V_{I}(t)\|=\|V(t)\|\le v$. The **interaction propagator** is
$$U_{I}(t,s):=E(-t)U(t,s)E(s)\qquad(s,t\in I),$$
and the model's clause (c)(ii) supplies, as the cited theorem proves, the decomposition
$$U(t,s)=E(t)U_{I}(t,s)E(-s).$$
The interaction propagator is unitary, jointly strongly continuous, satisfies $U_{I}(s,s)=I$ and the cocycle $U_{I}(t,r)=U_{I}(t,s)U_{I}(s,r)$, and its first-endpoint map is strongly differentiable with
$$i\hbar\,\partial_{t}U_{I}(t,s)\psi=V_{I}(t)U_{I}(t,s)\psi\qquad(\psi\in\mathfrak H),$$
all as supplied by [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-strong-bounded-interaction-picture]]; these are readings of that theorem in the model's vocabulary, not new assumptions.

**(c) Interaction states and preparations.** For a Schroedinger-picture state vector $\psi(t)=U(t,s)\psi(s)$ the **interaction-picture state** is
$$\psi_{I}(t):=E(-t)\psi(t),\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad\psi_{I}(t)=U_{I}(t,s)\psi_{I}(s),$$
and for a preparation $\rho$ with $\rho(t)=U(t,s)\rho(s)U(t,s)^{*}$ the **interaction-picture preparation** is
$$\rho_{I}(t):=E(-t)\rho(t)E(t),$$
which is again a preparation of the model by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]; for a pure preparation $[\psi(s)]$, $[\psi_{I}(t)]$ is pure. The map $\psi(t)\mapsto\psi_{I}(t)$ is unitary at every $t$, so $\|\psi_{I}(t)\|=\|\psi(t)\|$.

**(d) The two pictures assign the same outcome laws.** Let $(A,u_{A})$ be an assigned sharp observable with $A\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ bounded and let $A_{I}(t):=E(-t)AE(t)$ be its interaction-picture representative, which is again a bounded self-adjoint observable with $E_{A_{I}(t)}(B)=E(-t)E_{A}(B)E(t)$ for every Borel set $B$ by clause (d) of [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-flow]] applied to the flow $E$ of the self-adjoint $T=-H_{0}/\hbar$. Then for every preparation $\rho$ specified at $s$ and every $t\in I$,
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A_{I}(t)}_{\rho_{I}(t)}(B)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
because $\rho(t)=E(t)\rho_{I}(t)E(-t)$ and $\operatorname{tr}\bigl(E(t)\rho_{I}E(-t)E_{A}(B)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho_{I}E(-t)E_{A}(B)E(t)\bigr)$ by cyclicity of the trace; equivalently, for a pure preparation, $\|E_{A}(B)\psi(t)\|=\|E_{A_{I}(t)}(B)\psi_{I}(t)\|$. This identity is the precise sense in which the two pictures are two bookkeeping devices for the same model; it is a reading of P2 together with the cited mathematics, not a claim about apparatuses.

**(e) Energy-basis transition amplitudes.** Let $\varphi_{a},\varphi_{b}\in D(H_{0})$ be unit eigenvectors, $H_{0}\varphi_{a}=E_{a}\varphi_{a}$, $H_{0}\varphi_{b}=E_{b}\varphi_{b}$, and let $A_{ba}(t,s)$ and $p_{ba}(t,s)$ be the transition amplitude and probability of clause (e) of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]]. Then
$$A_{ba}(t,s)=e^{is(E_{a}-E_{b})/\hbar}\bigl\langle U_{I}(t,s)\varphi_{a},\varphi_{b}\bigr\rangle ,\qquad\text{hence}\qquad p_{ba}(t,s)=\bigl|\bigl\langle U_{I}(t,s)\varphi_{a},\varphi_{b}\bigr\rangle\bigr|^{2},$$
by the decomposition of clause (b) and $E(-s)\varphi_{a}=e^{isE_{a}/\hbar}\varphi_{a}$, $\langle E(t)\chi,\varphi_{b}\rangle=e^{-itE_{b}/\hbar}\langle\chi,\varphi_{b}\rangle$; the phases are of modulus one ([[def-inner-product-space]]). The transition probability is therefore computable in either picture, and the definition records this as the reading used by the page's amplitude theorem; no measurement frequency or rate is defined.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (b)-(e) are readings of the declared driven model, of clauses (b)-(e) of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]], and of P1 and P2, in the vocabulary of the cited mathematics. The interaction picture is a change of description of the same model: it adds no assumption, no physical process, no measurement and no empirical claim, and it asserts nothing about detectors, records or the laboratory realization of the model.

items.title: The two-level rotating frame: conjugation identities, the transformed families and invariance of the level populations
items.statement:
## Statement

Let $(\sigma_x,\sigma_y,\sigma_z)$ be the Pauli matrices of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e), acting on $\mathbb C^2$ in the orthonormal basis $(e_{\uparrow},e_{\downarrow})$ of that clause, so that $\sigma_z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$, $\sigma_x\sigma_y=i\sigma_z$, $\sigma_y\sigma_z=i\sigma_x$ and $\sigma_z\sigma_x=i\sigma_y$; write $I$ for the identity and let $P_{\uparrow},P_{\downarrow}$ be the orthogonal projections onto $\mathbb Ce_{\uparrow}$ and $\mathbb Ce_{\downarrow}$. Let $\hbar>0$, $\omega,\omega_0,\Omega_1\in\mathbb R$, put $\Delta:=\omega_0-\omega$ and, for $t\in\mathbb R$,
$$R(t):=\cos\!\Bigl(\frac{\omega t}{2}\Bigr)I+i\sin\!\Bigl(\frac{\omega t}{2}\Bigr)\sigma_z .$$
Then:

(a) *Frame.* For every $t$ the matrix $R(t)$ is unitary with $R(0)=I$, the map $R$ is of class $C^{\infty}$ with
$$R'(t)=\frac{i\omega}{2}\,\sigma_zR(t),$$
and $R(t)P_{\uparrow}R(t)^{*}=P_{\uparrow}$, $R(t)P_{\downarrow}R(t)^{*}=P_{\downarrow}$.

(b) *Conjugation.* For every $t$,
$$R(t)\sigma_xR(t)^{*}=\cos(\omega t)\,\sigma_x-\sin(\omega t)\,\sigma_y,\qquad R(t)\sigma_yR(t)^{*}=\sin(\omega t)\,\sigma_x+\cos(\omega t)\,\sigma_y,\qquad R(t)\sigma_zR(t)^{*}=\sigma_z .$$

(c) *Circular drive.* For the family $H_{\mathrm c}(t):=\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(\omega_0\sigma_z+\Omega_1(\cos(\omega t)\sigma_x+\sin(\omega t)\sigma_y)\bigr)$ one has, for every $t$,
$$R(t)H_{\mathrm c}(t)R(t)^{*}+i\hbar R'(t)R(t)^{*}=\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(\Delta\sigma_z+\Omega_1\sigma_x\bigr),$$
which is a constant Hermitian matrix independent of $t$.

(d) *Linear drive.* For the family $H_{\mathrm l}(t):=\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(\omega_0\sigma_z+\Omega_1\cos(\omega t)\sigma_x\bigr)$ put
$$A:=\frac{\hbar}{2}\Bigl(\Delta\sigma_z+\frac{\Omega_1}{2}\sigma_x\Bigr),\qquad B:=\frac{\hbar\Omega_1}{8}\bigl(\sigma_x+i\sigma_y\bigr).$$
Then for every $t$
$$R(t)H_{\mathrm l}(t)R(t)^{*}+i\hbar R'(t)R(t)^{*}=A+e^{2i\omega t}B+e^{-2i\omega t}B^{*},$$
and $\|A\|\le\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(|\Delta|+\frac{|\Omega_1|}{2}\bigr)$, $\|B\|=\frac{\hbar|\Omega_1|}{4}$.

(e) *Transformation of the dynamics.* Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H:\mathbb R\to\operatorname{End}(\mathbb C^2)$ be continuous with Hermitian values, let $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C^2$ be of class $C^1$ with
$$i\hbar\psi'(t)=H(t)\psi(t)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
and put $\psi_R:=R\psi$ and $H^{R}(t):=R(t)H(t)R(t)^{*}+i\hbar R'(t)R(t)^{*}$. Then $\psi_R$ is of class $C^1$ and satisfies $i\hbar\psi_R'(t)=H^{R}(t)\psi_R(t)$ for every $t$; the family $H^{R}$ is continuous with Hermitian values. Consequently, if $U$ is the unitary propagator of the norm-continuous family $H$ supplied by [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-norm-dyson-series-and-uniqueness]], then
$$U^{R}(t,s):=R(t)U(t,s)R(s)^{*}\qquad(s,t\in\mathbb R)$$
is the unitary propagator of $H^{R}$: it satisfies $i\hbar\partial_tU^{R}(t,s)=H^{R}(t)U^{R}(t,s)$, $U^{R}(s,s)=I$, the cocycle, and $U^{R}(t,s)^{*}=U^{R}(s,t)$. Moreover for every solution $\psi$ of the $H$-equation, every $t\in\mathbb R$ and both signs $\bullet\in\{\uparrow,\downarrow\}$,
$$\bigl\langle P_{\bullet}\psi(t),\psi(t)\bigr\rangle=\bigl\langle P_{\bullet}\psi_R(t),\psi_R(t)\bigr\rangle .$$

The lemma is a statement of finite-dimensional linear algebra and calculus for the displayed matrices; no physical identification, no measurement and no asymptotic claim is made.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the Pauli matrices $\sigma_x,\sigma_y,\sigma_z$ on $\mathbb C^2$ in the basis $(e_{\uparrow},e_{\downarrow})$; the projections $P_{\uparrow},P_{\downarrow}$; $\hbar>0$ and $\omega,\omega_0,\Omega_1,\Delta$; the matrix $R(t)$; the families $H_{\mathrm c},H_{\mathrm l}$ and the matrices $A,B$; where clause (e) is used, a continuous Hermitian family $H$ and a $C^1$ solution $\psi$, and Countable Choice.

[F1] **The Pauli matrices.** In the ordered basis $(e_{\uparrow},e_{\downarrow})$ one has $\sigma_x=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $\sigma_y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\ i&0\end{pmatrix}$, $\sigma_z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$, the matrices are Hermitian, $\sigma_x^2=\sigma_y^2=\sigma_z^2=I$, $\sigma_x\sigma_y=i\sigma_z$, $\sigma_y\sigma_z=i\sigma_x$, $\sigma_z\sigma_x=i\sigma_y$ and $\sigma_i\sigma_j+\sigma_j\sigma_i=2\delta_{ij}I$ for $i,j\in\{x,y,z\}$; products of matrices are computed entrywise-finitely ([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e)).

[F2] **Complex exponential and trigonometric functions.** For every real $\theta$, $e^{i\theta}=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta$, so $e^{i\theta}=\overline{e^{-i\theta}}$ ([[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]); $\sin'=\cos$ and $\cos'=-\sin$ with the chain rule for $t\mapsto\sin(\omega t)$, $t\mapsto\cos(\omega t)$ for constant $\omega$ ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]]); and the addition formulas $\cos(u+v)=\cos u\cos v-\sin u\sin v$, $\sin(u+v)=\sin u\cos v+\cos u\sin v$ hold for all real $u,v$, so in particular $\cos(2u)=\cos^{2}u-\sin^{2}u$, $\sin(2u)=2\sin u\cos u$ and $\cos^{2}u+\sin^{2}u=1$ ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-addition-formulas]]).

[F3] **The scalar product rule.** If $f,g:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ are differentiable at $t$ — the difference quotients of real and imaginary parts converge, equivalently $(f(t+h)-f(t))/h$ converges in $\mathbb C$ — then $fg$ is differentiable at $t$ with $(fg)'(t)=f'(t)g(t)+f(t)g'(t)$, and sums and constant multiples obey the same rule ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] applied to real and imaginary parts; [[def-derivative]]). Applying this to the finitely many entries of a product of $2\times2$ matrices whose entries are differentiable real functions of $t$ gives the entrywise product rule $(UV)'=U'V+UV'$ for such matrix curves.

[F4] **Unitary propagator of a norm-continuous bounded family.** If $H:\mathbb R\to\operatorname{End}(\mathbb C^2)$ is continuous with Hermitian values then it is norm-continuous with bounded self-adjoint values on every compact interval, and [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-norm-dyson-series-and-uniqueness]] supplies a unique family $U(t,s)$ of unitary matrices with $U(s,s)=I$, $U(t,s)U(s,r)=U(t,r)$, $U(t,s)^{*}=U(s,t)$, operator-norm continuity in $(t,s)$, and operator-norm derivative $\partial_tU(t,s)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}H(t)U(t,s)$; for fixed $s$ it is the unique norm-continuous solution of that equation with $U(s,s)=I$ ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-norm-dyson-series-and-uniqueness]] clauses (b), (c), (d); [[def-countable-choice]]).

[F5] **Inner product.** The pairing on $\mathbb C^2$ is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second, and $\langle Uu,Uv\rangle=\langle u,v\rangle$ for unitary $U$ ([[def-inner-product-space]]); with $\sigma_i$ as in [F1], the projections $P_{\uparrow}=\frac{1}{2}(I+\sigma_z)$ and $P_{\downarrow}=\frac{1}{2}(I-\sigma_z)$ satisfy $P^{2}=P=P^{*}$ and act as the orthogonal projections onto the displayed basis vectors.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; compute the displayed $2\times2$ matrices entrywise, differentiate the frame, and transform the differential equation by the product rule.

**Given:** the data of the Statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [The frame is a diagonal unitary] By [F1], $\sigma_z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$, so [F2] gives $$R(t)=\operatorname{diag}\bigl(e^{i\omega t/2},e^{-i\omega t/2}\bigr)$$ in the basis $(e_{\uparrow},e_{\downarrow})$; hence $R(t)^{*}=\overline{R(t)}=\operatorname{diag}\bigl(e^{-i\omega t/2},e^{i\omega t/2}\bigr)=R(t)^{-1}$ by [F2], so $R(t)$ is unitary with $R(t)R(t)^{*}=R(t)^{*}R(t)=I$ and $R(0)=I$. Since $R$ is diagonal, it commutes with the diagonal projections $P_{\uparrow}=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)$ and $P_{\downarrow}=\operatorname{diag}(0,1)$, so $R(t)P_{\bullet}R(t)^{*}=P_{\bullet}R(t)R(t)^{*}=P_{\bullet}$ for both signs. This proves the unitarity, the initial value and the projection identities of (a). [F1, F2, given, algebra]

1.2 [Derivative of the frame] By [F2] and the chain rule, the entries $t\mapsto e^{\pm i\omega t/2}$ have derivatives $\pm\frac{i\omega}{2}e^{\pm i\omega t/2}$, so $$R'(t)=\operatorname{diag}\Bigl(\frac{i\omega}{2}e^{i\omega t/2},-\frac{i\omega}{2}e^{-i\omega t/2}\Bigr)=\frac{i\omega}{2}\operatorname{diag}\bigl(e^{i\omega t/2},-e^{-i\omega t/2}\bigr).$$ Since $\sigma_zR(t)=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)\operatorname{diag}(e^{i\omega t/2},e^{-i\omega t/2})=\operatorname{diag}(e^{i\omega t/2},-e^{-i\omega t/2})$ by [F1] and entrywise matrix multiplication, $R'(t)=\frac{i\omega}{2}\sigma_zR(t)$, which completes (a). [F1, F2, algebra]

1.3 [Conjugation identities] Write $r_{\uparrow}:=e^{i\omega t/2}$, $r_{\downarrow}:=e^{-i\omega t/2}$, so $R=\operatorname{diag}(r_{\uparrow},r_{\downarrow})$. Multiplying the displayed $2\times2$ matrices [F1] entrywise, $$R\sigma_xR^{*}=\begin{pmatrix}0&r_{\uparrow}\overline{r_{\downarrow}}\\ r_{\downarrow}\overline{r_{\uparrow}}&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad R\sigma_yR^{*}=\begin{pmatrix}0&-ir_{\uparrow}\overline{r_{\downarrow}}\\ ir_{\downarrow}\overline{r_{\uparrow}}&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad R\sigma_zR^{*}=\sigma_z ,$$ because $\sigma_z$ is diagonal and commutes with $R$. By [F2], $r_{\uparrow}\overline{r_{\downarrow}}=e^{i\omega t/2}e^{i\omega t/2}=e^{i\omega t}=\cos(\omega t)+i\sin(\omega t)$ and $r_{\downarrow}\overline{r_{\uparrow}}=e^{-i\omega t}=\cos(\omega t)-i\sin(\omega t)$. Substituting, the first matrix equals $\cos(\omega t)\sigma_x-\sin(\omega t)\sigma_y$ and the second equals $\sin(\omega t)\sigma_x+\cos(\omega t)\sigma_y$, by the entries displayed in [F1]. This proves (b). [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 [The circular family] By step 1.3 and the linearity of matrix multiplication, $$R(t)\Bigl(\cos(\omega t)\sigma_x+\sin(\omega t)\sigma_y\Bigr)R(t)^{*}=\cos(\omega t)\bigl(\cos(\omega t)\sigma_x-\sin(\omega t)\sigma_y\bigr)+\sin(\omega t)\bigl(\sin(\omega t)\sigma_x+\cos(\omega t)\sigma_y\bigr)=\bigl(\cos^{2}(\omega t)+\sin^{2}(\omega t)\bigr)\sigma_x=\sigma_x ,$$ the $\sigma_y$ coefficients cancelling, and $\cos^{2}+\sin^{2}=1$ by [F2]. Since $R\sigma_zR^{*}=\sigma_z$ by step 1.3, $$R(t)H_{\mathrm c}(t)R(t)^{*}=\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(\omega_0\sigma_z+\Omega_1\sigma_x\bigr),$$ and by step 1.2, $i\hbar R'(t)R(t)^{*}=i\hbar\frac{i\omega}{2}\sigma_zR(t)R(t)^{*}=-\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\sigma_z$. Adding the two expressions gives $\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl((\omega_0-\omega)\sigma_z+\Omega_1\sigma_x\bigr)=\frac{\hbar}{2}(\Delta\sigma_z+\Omega_1\sigma_x)$, a constant Hermitian matrix because $\Delta,\Omega_1$ are real and the $\sigma_i$ are Hermitian [F1]. This is (c). [step 1.2, step 1.3, F1, F2, given, algebra]

2.2 [The linear family] Again by step 1.3 and [F2], $$R(t)\bigl(\cos(\omega t)\sigma_x\bigr)R(t)^{*}=\cos^{2}(\omega t)\sigma_x-\sin(\omega t)\cos(\omega t)\sigma_y=\frac{1+\cos(2\omega t)}{2}\sigma_x-\frac{\sin(2\omega t)}{2}\sigma_y ,$$ and $R\sigma_zR^{*}=\sigma_z$, so $$R(t)H_{\mathrm l}(t)R(t)^{*}+i\hbar R'(t)R(t)^{*}=\frac{\hbar}{2}\Bigl(\Delta\sigma_z+\frac{\Omega_1}{2}\sigma_x\Bigr)+\frac{\hbar\Omega_1}{4}\bigl(\cos(2\omega t)\sigma_x-\sin(2\omega t)\sigma_y\bigr)=A+\frac{\hbar\Omega_1}{4}\bigl(\cos(2\omega t)\sigma_x-\sin(2\omega t)\sigma_y\bigr).$$ By [F2], $e^{\pm 2i\omega t}=\cos(2\omega t)\pm i\sin(2\omega t)$, so with $B=\frac{\hbar\Omega_1}{8}(\sigma_x+i\sigma_y)$ one has $$e^{2i\omega t}B+e^{-2i\omega t}B^{*}=\frac{\hbar\Omega_1}{8}\Bigl(e^{2i\omega t}(\sigma_x+i\sigma_y)+e^{-2i\omega t}(\sigma_x-i\sigma_y)\Bigr)=\frac{\hbar\Omega_1}{8}\Bigl(2\cos(2\omega t)\sigma_x-2\sin(2\omega t)\sigma_y\Bigr),$$ which is the displayed remainder; hence the factorised form of (d). Finally $\|A\|=\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl\|\Delta\sigma_z+\frac{\Omega_1}{2}\sigma_x\bigr\|\le\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(|\Delta|+\frac{|\Omega_1|}{2}\bigr)$ because $\sigma_z,\sigma_x$ are Hermitian unitaries [F1], and $\|\sigma_x+i\sigma_y\|=\|2\sigma_+\|=2$ since $\sigma_x+i\sigma_y=\begin{pmatrix}0&2\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$ has operator norm $2$ by [F1]; hence $\|B\|=\frac{\hbar|\Omega_1|}{8}\cdot2=\frac{\hbar|\Omega_1|}{4}$. This is (d). [step 1.2, step 1.3, F1, F2, algebra]

2.3 [Transformation of the equation] Let $H$ and $\psi$ be as in clause (e) and let $t\in\mathbb R$. The entries of $R$ are $C^{\infty}$ by step 1.1 and [F2], those of $\psi$ are $C^1$ by hypothesis, so by the entrywise product rule [F3] the product $\psi_R=R\psi$ is $C^1$ with $$\psi_R'(t)=R'(t)\psi(t)+R(t)\psi'(t)=\frac{i\omega}{2}\sigma_zR(t)\psi(t)+R(t)\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}H(t)\psi(t)\Bigr),$$ using step 1.2 and the equation $i\hbar\psi'=H\psi$. Multiplying by $i\hbar$, $$i\hbar\psi_R'(t)=\Bigl(-\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\sigma_z+R(t)H(t)R(t)^{*}\Bigr)\psi_R(t)=H^{R}(t)\psi_R(t) ,$$ since $R(t)^{*}=R(t)^{-1}$ by step 1.1 and $i\hbar R'(t)R(t)^{*}=-\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\sigma_z$ by step 1.2; the family $H^{R}$ is continuous with Hermitian values because $R$ is continuous unitary, $H$ is continuous Hermitian and $i\hbar R'R^{*}=-\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\sigma_z$ is constant Hermitian. This proves the first assertion of (e). [step 1.1, step 1.2, F3, given, algebra]

2.4 [The transformed propagator] Let $U$ be the propagator of [F4]. By [F4] and step 1.1, $U^{R}(t,s)=R(t)U(t,s)R(s)^{*}$ is unitary, $U^{R}(s,s)=R(s)R(s)^{*}=I$, and the cocycle and adjoint identities follow from those of $U$ and $R$. For the derivative, [F4] gives operator-norm differentiability of $U(\cdot,s)$, so by the entrywise product rule [F3] applied to the entries of $R(t)U(t,s)R(s)^{*}$, $$\partial_tU^{R}(t,s)=R'(t)U(t,s)R(s)^{*}+R(t)\partial_tU(t,s)R(s)^{*}=\frac{i\omega}{2}\sigma_zU^{R}(t,s)-\frac{i}{\hbar}R(t)H(t)U(t,s)R(s)^{*}=\frac{i\omega}{2}\sigma_zU^{R}(t,s)-\frac{i}{\hbar}R(t)H(t)R(t)^{*}U^{R}(t,s) ,$$ using step 1.2 and $R(t)R(t)^{*}=I$; multiplying by $i\hbar$ gives $i\hbar\partial_tU^{R}(t,s)=\bigl(R(t)H(t)R(t)^{*}-\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\sigma_z\bigr)U^{R}(t,s)=H^{R}(t)U^{R}(t,s)$ by step 1.1 and the definition of $H^{R}$. Since $U^{R}(\cdot,s)$ is continuous with $U^{R}(s,s)=I$ and $H^{R}$ is norm-continuous with Hermitian values, [F4] identifies $U^{R}(\cdot,s)$ with the unique propagator of $H^{R}$, so all conclusions of the "consequently" clause hold. [step 1.1, step 1.2, F3, F4, given, algebra]

3.1 [Invariance of the level populations] Let $\psi$ be a solution of the $H$-equation and $t\in\mathbb R$. By step 2.3, $\psi(t)=R(t)^{*}\psi_R(t)$; since $R(t)$ is unitary [F5] and $R(t)P_{\bullet}R(t)^{*}=P_{\bullet}$ by step 1.1, $$\bigl\langle P_{\bullet}\psi(t),\psi(t)\bigr\rangle=\bigl\langle P_{\bullet}R(t)^{*}\psi_R(t),R(t)^{*}\psi_R(t)\bigr\rangle=\bigl\langle R(t)P_{\bullet}R(t)^{*}\psi_R(t),\psi_R(t)\bigr\rangle=\bigl\langle P_{\bullet}\psi_R(t),\psi_R(t)\bigr\rangle ,$$ for both signs. This is the final assertion of (e). [step 1.1, step 2.3, F5, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **Where the two polarizations differ.** For the circular family the transformed generator is the constant matrix $\frac{\hbar}{2}(\Delta\sigma_z+\Omega_1\sigma_x)$; for the linear family it is its averaged constant matrix $A$, with transverse coefficient $\Omega_1/2$, plus the explicitly displayed counter-rotating term $e^{2i\omega t}B+e^{-2i\omega t}B^{*}$, which is the term dropped in a rotating-wave approximation. The lemma proves the exact identity; the size of the dropped term is bounded on the page that uses it.
- **No assumption on the sign of $\omega$.** The identities hold for every real $\omega$, including $\omega=0$, where $R\equiv I$ and the transformation is trivial; the matrix $H_{\mathrm c}$ reduces to $\frac{\hbar}{2}(\omega_0\sigma_z+\Omega_1\sigma_x)$ in that case.

items.title: The bounded norm-continuous driven model: unique unitary propagator, Dyson truncation budget and outcome-law error
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the framework data and the declared driven model of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] in the **bounded norm-continuous class** of clause (b)(i): $I=[a,b]$ is the declared compact time interval, $\mathfrak H$ the state space of the declared system, $\hbar>0$, and $H:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is norm-continuous with self-adjoint values, $K:=\sup_{t\in I}\|H(t)\|/\hbar<\infty$. Let $U_{0}(t,s)=I$ and $U_{n+1}(t,s)=\int_{s}^{t}A(r)U_{n}(r,s)\,dr$ with $A(r)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}H(r)$ be the oriented Dyson iterates of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-norm-dyson-series-and-uniqueness]], and let $U(t,s)=\sum_{n\ge0}U_{n}(t,s)$ be its norm-convergent propagator; for $N\in\mathbb N_{0}$ put $R_{N}(t,s):=U(t,s)-\sum_{n=0}^{N}U_{n}(t,s)$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the latter for the outcome-law reading of P2. Then:

(a) *Well-posedness of the declared model.* The family $U$ is the unique family of bounded operators on $\mathfrak H$ that is jointly norm-continuous on $I\times I$, unitary-valued, satisfies $U(s,s)=I$ and the cocycle $U(t,r)=U(t,s)U(s,r)$, and solves $i\hbar\partial_{t}U(t,s)=H(t)U(t,s)$ together with its second-endpoint equation $i\hbar\partial_{s}U(t,s)=-U(t,s)H(s)$ in operator norm. In particular the model's clause (c)(i) declaration has exactly one solution: the driven model in the bounded norm-continuous class is well posed.

(b) *Truncation budget.* For all $s,t\in I$ and all $N\in\mathbb N_{0}$, with $\tau:=|t-s|$,
$$\bigl\|R_{N}(t,s)\bigr\|\le e^{K\tau}\,\frac{(K\tau)^{N+1}}{(N+1)!},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \|U(t,s)-I\|\le e^{K\tau}-1 .$$
In particular $\|R_{1}(t,s)\|\le e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^{2}/2$ and $\|R_{2}(t,s)\|\le e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^{3}/6$.

(c) *Evolved states and outcome laws.* For every preparation $\rho$ specified at time $s$ the operator $\rho(t):=U(t,s)\rho(s)U(t,s)^{*}$ is a preparation of the model with $\operatorname{tr}\rho(t)=1$ for every $t\in I$, and the specification is consistent with the cocycle: evolving first from $s$ to $r$ and then from $r$ to $t$ gives the same preparation. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi(s)$ the vector $\psi(t):=U(t,s)\psi(s)$ is unit and spans a pure preparation for every $t$. For every assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]) and every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$, the number $\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)$ is the model's outcome probability at time $t$.

(d) *Error of the unnormalized truncated quadratic estimate.* Let $\psi(s)$ be a unit vector, put $\psi^{N}(t):=\sum_{n=0}^{N}U_{n}(t,s)\psi(s)$ and let $(A,u_{A})$ be an assigned sharp observable with $A\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ bounded. Then for every $t\in I$ and every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$\bigl|\mu^{A}_{\psi(t)}(B)-\mu^{A}_{\psi^{N}(t)}(B)\bigr|\le (1+\|\sum_{n=0}^NU_n(t,s)\|)\,\|R_N(t,s)\|\le 2\,e^{K\tau}\frac{(K\tau)^{N+1}}{(N+1)!},$$
where the truncated quantity is the unnormalized quadratic form $\mu^{A}_{\psi^{N}(t)}(B):=\|E_{A}(B)\psi^{N}(t)\|^{2}$ of the truncated vector, whose norm is at most $e^{K\tau}$. It is an approximation to the normalized exact Born law and need not itself be a probability law; for $N=1$ the right side is $2e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^{2}$.

(e) *Scope.* The theorem is conditional on the bounded norm-continuous class, on the compactness of $I$ and on $K<\infty$. It asserts no existence or uniqueness statement for unbounded families (which are treated in their own classes), no uniform-in-time approximation, no rate or decay, no measurement or apparatus model, and no comparison with any recorded data.

## Facts & Assumptions


**Given:** the declared driven model in the bounded norm-continuous class; the iteration $U_{n}$ with $A=-iH/\hbar$ and the propagator $U$; a truncation order $N$; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice.

[F1] **Dyson propagator.** Under the hypotheses of the Statement, $\|U_{n}(t,s)\|\le(K|t-s|)^{n}/n!$; the series $U=\sum_{n\ge0}U_{n}$ converges in operator norm uniformly on $I\times I$, is jointly norm-continuous, satisfies $U(s,s)=I$, $\|U(t,s)-I\|\le e^{K|t-s|}-1$, is the unique continuous $\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$-valued solution of the integral equation $U(t,s)=I-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_{s}^{t}H(r)U(r,s)\,dr$ for fixed $s$, and has operator-norm derivatives $\partial_{t}U(t,s)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}H(t)U(t,s)$, $\partial_{s}U(t,s)=+\frac{i}{\hbar}U(t,s)H(s)$; every $U(t,s)$ is unitary with $U(t,s)^{*}=U(s,t)$ and the cocycle holds ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-norm-dyson-series-and-uniqueness]] clauses (a)-(d)).

[F2] **Dyson truncation bound.** With the notation of [F1] and $R_{N}(t,s)=U(t,s)-\sum_{n=0}^{N}U_{n}(t,s)$ one has $\|R_{N}(t,s)\|\le e^{K|t-s|}(K|t-s|)^{N+1}/(N+1)!$ for all $s,t\in I$ and all $N$, and the same actual self-adjoint hypotheses give the stronger $\|R_N(t,s)\|\le(K\tau)^{N+1}/(N+1)!$ ([[lem-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-dyson-truncation-bound]] clause (b)).

[F3] **State and outcome readings of the model.** The model declares the evolved preparation $\rho(t)=U(t,s)\rho(s)U(t,s)^{*}$ and states that it is a preparation for every $t$ by unitarity and [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]; the outcome law of an assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ in a preparation is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{A}(B))$, for a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$ the value $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$ ([[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] clauses (c)(i), (d); [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a), (b); [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]; [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]; [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]).

[F4] **Inner-product and projection estimates.** The pairing is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second with $|\langle u,v\rangle|\le\|u\|\|v\|$ ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-for-real-and-complex-inner-product-spaces]], [[def-inner-product-space]]); the spectral projections $E_{A}(B)$ of a self-adjoint bounded $A$ satisfy $0\le E_{A}(B)\le I$ and $\|E_{A}(B)\|\le1$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]); and for unit vectors $u,v$ and a contraction $Q$ one has $|\|Qu\|^{2}-\|Qv\|^{2}|\le 2\|u-v\|$.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; instantiate the norm-continuous Dyson supplier and its truncation lemma at the model's data, then estimate the Born probabilities of the exact and truncated vectors.

**Given:** the data of the Statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [Well-posedness and the properties of the propagator] The family $H$ is norm-continuous with bounded self-adjoint values on the compact interval $I$, so [F1] applies and supplies the norm-convergent unitary propagator $U$ with the cocycle, the inverse relation, joint norm-continuity and the two operator-norm endpoint equations; uniqueness of the continuous solution of the integral equation with $U(s,s)=I$ for fixed $s$ is clause (c) of [F1], and the differential equation together with $U(s,s)=I$ implies that integral equation by integration. Hence the family declared in clause (c)(i) of the model is exactly $U$, and it is unique; this is clause (a). [F1, given]

1.2 [Truncation budget] By [F2] with $\tau=|t-s|$, $\|R_{N}(t,s)\|\le e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^{N+1}/(N+1)!$ for every $N\ge0$; the case $N=0$ gives $\|U(t,s)-I\|\le e^{K\tau}-1$, and $N=1$, $N=2$ give the displayed bounds. This is clause (b). [F2, algebra]

1.3 [Evolved preparations and outcome laws] By [F3] the model's evolved preparation is $\rho(t)=U(t,s)\rho(s)U(t,s)^{*}$, and it is a preparation for every $t$ because $U(t,s)$ is unitary [F1]; the cocycle of [F1] gives $U(t,r)\rho(r)U(t,r)^{*}=U(t,s)U(s,r)\rho(s)U(s,r)^{*}U(t,s)^{*}=\rho(t)$ for $r$ between $s$ and $t$, so the result does not depend on the intermediate time. For a unit vector $\psi(s)$, $\|\psi(t)\|=\|\psi(s)\|=1$ by unitarity, so $[\psi(t)]$ is a pure preparation. The outcome probability at time $t$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)$ by [F3], the reading of P2. This is clause (c). [F1, F3, given]

2.1 [Error of the unnormalized truncated estimate] Let $S_N=\sum_{n=0}^NU_n(t,s)$, $u=U(t,s)\psi(s)$ and $v=S_N\psi(s)$ for a unit initial vector. Then $\|u\|=1$, $\|v\|\le\|S_N\|\le\sum_{n=0}^N(K\tau)^n/n!\le e^{K\tau}$ by [F1], and $\|u-v\|\le\|R_N\|$. For the spectral projection $Q=E_A(B)$, the exact Born probability is $\|Qu\|^2$ while $\|Qv\|^2$ is the stated unnormalized quadratic estimate. Their difference equals $\langle Q(u-v),Qu\rangle+\langle Qv,Q(u-v)\rangle$; Cauchy-Schwarz and contraction of $Q$ bound its absolute value by $(1+\|S_N\|)\|R_N\|\le(1+e^{K\tau})\|R_N\|$. Crucially [F2] supplies the stronger unitary remainder $\|R_N\|\le(K\tau)^{N+1}/(N+1)!$, so the result is at most $2e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^{N+1}/(N+1)!$, preserving the advertised final bound. For $N=1$ it is at most $e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^2$, and hence also the stated looser $2e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^2$. At $K\tau=0$ both quantities coincide. No unit norm or density interpretation is assigned to the truncated vector. This proves (d). [step 1.1, step 1.2, F1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

3.1 [Scope] Only the bounded norm-continuous class, the compactness of $I$ and $K<\infty$ entered; the truncation bound is linear-exponential in $\tau$ and gives no uniform-in-time statement, the truncation is a mathematical error budget rather than a laboratory protocol, and no measurement, rate, decay or empirical comparison is asserted. This is clause (e). [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 2.1, given] ∎

## Remarks

- **The stronger unitary bound.** Because every $U(t,s)$ is unitary, the truncation lemma also records the bound $\|R_{N}(t,s)\|\le(K\tau)^{N+1}/(N+1)!$, which does not grow exponentially; the theorem states the exponential version because it is the one used to convert to the outcome-law estimate with the same constant.
- **From propagator error to probability error.** Clause (d) is the mechanism by which the Dyson truncation of the page's amplitude theorems becomes a bound on an outcome probability; it applies to every Borel outcome set and every bounded assigned sharp observable, and it requires no additional physical assumption beyond P2.

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Section 2.3 printed pages 15-17 (PDF pages 15-17): the time-ordered exponential series of a time-dependent Hamiltonian and its truncation

items.physical_scope: The bounded norm-continuous driven model of the declared system: existence, uniqueness and unitarity of the two-time propagator with its operator-norm Schroedinger equation, the Dyson truncation bound as an explicit error budget for the truncated propagator, the reading of evolved preparations at the running time, and the bound comparing exact Born probabilities to unnormalized truncated quadratic estimates. The theorem is conditional on the bounded norm-continuous class; it asserts no unbounded or common-domain family, no laboratory realization, no measurement model, no long-time limit and no empirical result.

items.title: The bounded-control driven model: mild propagator, interaction-picture evolution and equivalence of the two readings
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the framework data and the declared driven model of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] in the **bounded-control class** of clause (b)(ii): $\mathfrak H$ is the model's state space, $H_{0}$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), $V:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is strongly continuous with self-adjoint values and $v:=\sup_{t\in I}\|V(t)\|<\infty$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]), $H(t)=H_{0}+V(t)$ on $D(H_{0})$, and adopt the interaction-picture readings of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-interaction-picture]]: $E(t)=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}$, $V_{I}(t)=E(-t)V(t)E(t)$, $U_{I}(t,s)=E(-t)U(t,s)E(s)$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the latter for the outcome-law reading of P2. Let $U(t,s)$ be the mild propagator constructed by [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-strong-bounded-interaction-picture]]. Then:

(a) *Well-posedness of the declared model.* $U$ is the unique family of unitary operators on $\mathfrak H$, jointly strongly continuous on $I\times I$, with $U(s,s)=I$, $U(t,s)^{*}=U(s,t)$ and the cocycle $U(t,r)=U(t,s)U(s,r)$, satisfying the vectorwise mild Schroedinger identity
$$U(t,s)\psi=E(t-s)\psi-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_{s}^{t}E(t-r)V(r)U(r,s)\psi\,dr\qquad(\psi\in\mathfrak H,\ s,t\in I);$$
so the model's clause (c)(ii) declaration has exactly one solution. For $\psi,\varphi\in D(H_{0})$ the scalar curve $t\mapsto\langle U(t,s)\psi,\varphi\rangle$ is continuously differentiable on $I$ with
$$\frac{d}{dt}\bigl\langle U(t,s)\psi,\varphi\bigr\rangle=-\frac{i}{\hbar}\Bigl[\bigl\langle U(t,s)\psi,H_{0}\varphi\bigr\rangle+\bigl\langle V(t)U(t,s)\psi,\varphi\bigr\rangle\Bigr].$$
No invariance of $D(H_{0})$ under $U$, no strong full Schroedinger equation for its domain vectors, and no operator-norm differentiability of $U$ with respect to the unbounded generator are asserted.

(b) *Interaction picture.* For every $s,t\in I$ and every $\psi\in\mathfrak H$ the interaction state $\psi_{I}(t):=E(-t)U(t,s)\psi(s)$ satisfies $\psi_{I}(t)=U_{I}(t,s)\psi_{I}(s)$, and its first-endpoint map is strongly differentiable with $i\hbar\partial_{t}\psi_{I}(t)=V_{I}(t)\psi_{I}(t)$; the interaction propagator is unitary with the cocycle and $U_{I}(t,s)^{*}=U_{I}(s,t)$, and its strong truncation bound is $\|U_{I}(t,s)-\sum_{n=0}^{N}D_{n}(t,s)\|\le e^{K(t-s)}(K(t-s))^{N+1}/(N+1)!$ for $s\le t$ with $K=v/\hbar$.

(c) *Equivalence of the two readings.* For every preparation $\rho$ specified at time $s$, every assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ with $A$ bounded, every $t\in I$ and every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$, the Schroedinger reading and the interaction reading give the same outcome probability:
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A_{I}(t)}_{\rho_{I}(t)}(B),\qquad A_{I}(t)=E(-t)AE(t),\quad \rho_{I}(t)=E(-t)\rho(t)E(t),$$
and for pure preparations $\|\psi_{I}(t)\|=\|\psi(t)\|=\|\psi(s)\|$. For eigenvectors $\varphi_{a},\varphi_{b}$ of $H_{0}$ as in clause (e) of the model, the transition probabilities of the two pictures agree,
$$p_{ba}(t,s)=\bigl|\bigl\langle U(t,s)\varphi_{a},\varphi_{b}\bigr\rangle\bigr|^{2}=\bigl|\bigl\langle U_{I}(t,s)\varphi_{a},\varphi_{b}\bigr\rangle\bigr|^{2}.$$

(d) *Scope.* The theorem is conditional on the bounded-control class; the mild identity, not a strong equation on $D(H_{0})$, is the evolution equation it establishes, and it asserts nothing about unbounded controls, invariant domains, measurement records, detectors, rates or empirical data.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the declared driven model in the bounded-control class and its interaction-picture readings; the operators $E(t)$, $V_{I}$, $U_{I}$; a preparation $\rho$, a bounded assigned sharp observable $A$, times $s,t\in I$; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice.

[F1] **Interaction-picture supplier.** Under the hypotheses of the Statement, $V_{I}$ is strongly continuous with self-adjoint values and $\|V_{I}(t)\|=\|V(t)\|\le v$; the strong integrals $D_{n}(t,s)$ and the interaction propagator $U_{I}=\sum_{n\ge0}D_{n}$ converge in operator norm uniformly on the time triangle with $\|D_{n}\|\le(K(t-s))^{n}/n!$ and $\|U_{I}(t,s)-\sum_{n=0}^{N}D_{n}\|\le e^{K(t-s)}(K(t-s))^{N+1}/(N+1)!$; $U_{I}$ extends to all $s,t\in I$ as a strongly continuous unitary evolution with $U_{I}(s,t)=U_{I}(t,s)^{-1}=U_{I}(t,s)^{*}$ and the cocycle; for every $\psi$ its first-endpoint map is $C^{1}$ with $U_{I}(t,s)\psi=\psi+\int_{s}^{t}B(r)U_{I}(r,s)\psi\,dr$ and $\partial_{t}U_{I}(t,s)\psi=B(t)U_{I}(t,s)\psi$, where $B(t)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}V_{I}(t)$; the physical propagator $U(t,s)=E(t)U_{I}(t,s)E(-s)$ is unitary, jointly strongly continuous, has the cocycle and inverse, and satisfies the vectorwise mild identity $U(t,s)\psi=E(t-s)\psi-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_{s}^{t}E(t-r)V(r)U(r,s)\psi\,dr$; for $\psi,\varphi\in D(H_{0})$ the scalar curve satisfies $\frac{d}{dt}\langle U(t,s)\psi,\varphi\rangle=-\frac{i}{\hbar}[\langle U(t,s)\psi,H_{0}\varphi\rangle+\langle V(t)U(t,s)\psi,\varphi\rangle]$ ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-strong-bounded-interaction-picture]]).

[F2] **Model and picture readings.** The model declares $U$ of clause (c)(ii) as the propagator carrying the state evolution and fixes the evolved preparation and outcome-law readings ([[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] clauses (c)(ii), (d)); the interaction-picture readings fix $E,V_{I},U_{I},\psi_{I},\rho_{I}$ and state the outcome-law equivalence with the conjugate observable $A_{I}(t)=E(-t)AE(t)$ ([[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-interaction-picture]] clauses (b)-(e)). The conjugate observable has spectral measure $E_{A_{I}(t)}(B)=E(-t)E_{A}(B)E(t)$ ([[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-flow]] clause (d), applied to the flow $E$ of the self-adjoint generator $-H_{0}/\hbar$).

[F3] **Framework readings.** $\rho(t)=U(t,s)\rho(s)U(t,s)^{*}$ is a preparation and the outcome law of an assigned sharp observable in a preparation is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$ with the pure form $\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a), (b); [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]; [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]; [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]); $E(t)=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}$ is the autonomous flow of the assigned energy observable $(H_{0},\mathrm J)$ ([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (b)).

[F4] **Inner product.** The pairing is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second, and unitary operators preserve it ([[def-inner-product-space]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; instantiate the interaction-picture supplier at the model's data and transfer the model's readings through the recorded definitions.

**Given:** the data of the Statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [Well-posedness and the mild identity] The pair $(H_{0},V)$ satisfies exactly the hypotheses of [F1] and the model's clause (b)(ii) is that hypothesis, so [F1] supplies the family $U(t,s)=E(t)U_{I}(t,s)E(-s)$ with the unitary, strong-continuity, inverse and cocycle properties and the vectorwise mild identity, and identifies it with the solution of the model's clause (c)(ii); the uniqueness is the uniqueness of $U_{I}$ as the norm-convergent Dyson sum of [F1], since $E$ is a fixed unitary family. The weak identity for $\psi,\varphi\in D(H_{0})$ is the scalar derivative assertion of [F1]. This is clause (a). [F1, F2, given]

1.2 [Interaction picture] By [F1], $U_{I}$ is unitary with the cocycle and adjoint properties, its first-endpoint map is strongly $C^{1}$ with $i\hbar\partial_{t}U_{I}(t,s)=V_{I}(t)U_{I}(t,s)$, and the truncation bound is displayed; by [F2] $\psi_{I}(t)=E(-t)\psi(t)$ and $\psi_{I}(t)=U_{I}(t,s)\psi_{I}(s)$, so the strong equation for $\psi_{I}$ follows from the equation for $U_{I}$ applied to $\psi_{I}(s)$. This is clause (b). [F1, F2, given]

1.3 [Equivalence of the readings] Let $\rho$ be specified at $s$ and let $A$ be bounded. By [F2], $\rho_{I}(t)=E(-t)\rho(t)E(t)$ and $E_{A_{I}(t)}(B)=E(-t)E_{A}(B)E(t)$; using $\rho(t)=E(t)\rho_{I}(t)E(-t)$ and the trace identity $\operatorname{tr}(E(t)\rho_{I}E(-t)E_{A}(B))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{I}E(-t)E_{A}(B)E(t))$, the two laws agree; for pure preparations unitarity of $E(-t)$ [F4] gives $\|\psi_{I}(t)\|=\|\psi(t)\|=\|\psi(s)\|$ by [F1]. For the eigenvector amplitudes, $U=E(t)U_{I}E(-s)$ and $E(\pm t)\varphi_{a/b}=e^{\mp itE_{a/b}/\hbar}\varphi_{a/b}$, so the two inner products differ by the phase $e^{is(E_{a}-E_{b})/\hbar}$ of modulus one and the transition probabilities agree, as recorded in clause (e) of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-interaction-picture]]. This is clause (c). [F1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 [Scope] Every hypothesis used is one of: self-adjointness of $H_{0}$, strong continuity and boundedness of the self-adjoint control, the compactness of $I$, and the choice hypotheses; the established equation is the mild identity, and no invariance of $D(H_{0})$, no strong equation for its vectors, no measurement and no empirical claim entered, which is clause (d). [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, given] ∎

## Remarks

- **Why the mild equation and not more.** The supplier deliberately does not claim that $U(t,s)$ maps $D(H_{0})$ into itself, so the strong full Schroedinger equation for domain vectors is not available at this level of hypothesis; the weak identity of clause (a) is what remains, and it is enough for the amplitude theorem of this page because the eigenvector amplitudes are evaluated in the energy basis of $H_{0}$.
- **The interaction picture does not change the model.** Clause (c) records that $A$ and $\rho$ are transported together; a computation in the interaction picture is therefore a computation of the same outcome law, not a different physical situation.

The theorem is conditional on a self-adjoint H0 and a strongly continuous bounded self-adjoint control and asserts no invariant domain, no strong full Schroedinger equation for domain vectors, no measurement and no empirical result.

items.title: First-order transition amplitudes for a bounded control: Dyson remainder, the sinusoidal drive with its co- and counter-rotating parts, and the outcome-probability error
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the framework data and the declared driven model of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] in the **bounded-control class** of clause (b)(ii): $\mathfrak H$ is the model's state space, $H_{0}$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$, $V:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is strongly continuous with self-adjoint values, $v=\sup_{t\in I}\|V(t)\|<\infty$ and $H(t)=H_{0}+V(t)$; let $U(t,s)$ be the mild propagator and put $K:=v/\hbar$. Let $(\varphi_{j})_{j\in J}$ be an orthonormal family in $D(H_{0})$ with $H_{0}\varphi_{j}=E_{j}\varphi_{j}$ ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]) — a complete family is not required — and fix labels $i,j\in J$ and $s\le t$ in $I$, with $\tau:=t-s$ and $\Delta:=E_{j}-E_{i}$. Let $A_{ji}(t,s)=e^{iE_j\tau/\hbar}\langle U(t,s)\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\rangle$ be the transition amplitude of clause (e) of the model and define its first-order term
$$A^{(1)}_{ji}(t,s):=-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_{s}^{t}e^{i\Delta(r-s)/\hbar}\bigl\langle V(r)\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\bigr\rangle\,dr .$$
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) *Exact amplitude with Dyson remainder.* There is a remainder $R_{ji}(t,s)$ with
$$A_{ji}(t,s)=\delta_{ij}+A^{(1)}_{ji}(t,s)+R_{ji}(t,s),\qquad |R_{ji}(t,s)|\le e^{K\tau}\frac{(K\tau)^{2}}{2},$$
and if $\|V(r)-V_{0}(r)\|\le\eta(r)$ for a family $V_{0}$ of self-adjoint bounded operators with integrable scalar coefficient $r\mapsto\langle V_{0}(r)\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\rangle$, then the corresponding first-order amplitude differs from $A^{(1)}_{ji}$ by at most $\frac{1}{\hbar}\int_{s}^{t}\eta(r)\,dr$.

(b) *Sinusoidal control.* Let $W\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ be self-adjoint, $\omega,\vartheta\in\mathbb R$, and suppose $V(r)=W\cos(\omega r+\vartheta)$ for $r\in I$. Put $\vartheta_{0}:=\omega s+\vartheta$ and decompose
$$A^{(1)}_{ji}=a_{+}+a_{-},\qquad a_{\pm}:=-\frac{i}{2\hbar}\bigl\langle W\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\bigr\rangle e^{\mp i\vartheta_{0}}\,\frac{e^{i(\Delta\mp\hbar\omega)\tau/\hbar}-1}{i(\Delta\mp\hbar\omega)/\hbar},$$
with the convention that the quotient is the limit $\tau$ when $\Delta\mp\hbar\omega=0$. Then the *co-rotating* term $a_{+}$ (the one whose denominator vanishes at $\Delta=\hbar\omega$) satisfies
$$|a_{+}|=\bigl|\bigl\langle W\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\bigr\rangle\bigr|\,\frac{\bigl|\sin\bigl((\Delta-\hbar\omega)\tau/(2\hbar)\bigr)\bigr|}{|\Delta-\hbar\omega|},\qquad\text{and at }\Delta=\hbar\omega:\quad |a_{+}|=\bigl|\bigl\langle W\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\bigr\rangle\bigr|\frac{\tau}{2\hbar},$$
and the *counter-rotating* term satisfies $|a_{-}|\le|\langle W\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\rangle|/|\Delta+\hbar\omega|$ whenever $\Delta+\hbar\omega\ne0$.

(c) *Outcome probability.* The model's transition probability is $p_{ji}(t,s)=|A_{ji}(t,s)|^{2}$; with $\varepsilon:=e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^{2}/2$ and $A^{(1)}:=A^{(1)}_{ji}$, for distinct labels $i\ne j$
$$\bigl|p_{ji}(t,s)-|A^{(1)}|^{2}\bigr|\le 2|A^{(1)}|\,\varepsilon+\varepsilon^{2},$$
and for $i=j$ the survival probability obeys the analogous bound $\bigl|p_{ii}(t,s)-|1+A^{(1)}|^{2}\bigr|\le(2+2|A^{(1)}|)\varepsilon+\varepsilon^{2}$; in both cases the exact outcome probability is controlled by the first-order term and the explicit Dyson error of clause (a).

(d) *Scope.* The statements are finite-time and conditional on the bounded control and on the orthonormal eigenfamily; the remainder bound grows like $\tau^{2}e^{K\tau}$ and no long-time limit, transition rate, exponential decay, continuum density of states or Fermi golden rule is asserted, and no measured frequency, count or rate is claimed.

## Facts & Assumptions


**Given:** the declared driven model in the bounded-control class; the orthonormal eigenfamily $(\varphi_{j})$ with $H_{0}\varphi_{j}=E_{j}\varphi_{j}$; labels $i,j$, times $s\le t$, $\tau=t-s$, $\Delta=E_{j}-E_{i}$, $K=v/\hbar$; where clause (b) applies, $W,\omega,\vartheta$ with $V(r)=W\cos(\omega r+\vartheta)$; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice.

[F1] **Amplitude supplier.** Under the hypotheses of the Statement, with $(\varphi_{n})$ a complete orthonormal family of $H_{0}$-eigenvectors and $A_{b_{0}a_{0}}(t,s)$ as defined in clause (e) of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]], one has $A_{b_{0}a_{0}}=\delta_{a_{0}b_{0}}-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_{s}^{t}e^{i(E_{b_{0}}-E_{a_{0}})(r-s)/\hbar}\langle V(r)\varphi_{a_{0}},\varphi_{b_{0}}\rangle dr+R_{b_{0}a_{0}}$ with $|R_{b_{0}a_{0}}|\le e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^{2}/2$; and if $\|V(r)-V_{0}(r)\|\le\eta(r)$ with measurable integrable coefficient, the amplitude computed with $V_{0}$ differs from the exact one by at most $\frac{1}{\hbar}\int_{s}^{t}\eta(r)dr+e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^{2}/2$ ([[prop-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-first-order-amplitude-tail]]). The proof of that item uses only the two fixed basis vectors, so the completeness of the eigenfamily is not needed for the displayed conclusion on the pair $(i,j)$.

[F2] **Model and picture readings.** The model defines the amplitude $A_{ji}=e^{iE_j\tau/\hbar}\langle U(t,s)\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\rangle$ and the probability $p_{ji}=|A_{ji}|^{2}$, with the reading of the outcome law of the energy observable in clause (e) ([[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] clauses (c)(ii), (e)); the physical propagator is the mild propagator of the bounded-control class ([[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-mild-propagator-and-pictures]] clauses (a), (b); [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-strong-bounded-interaction-picture]]; [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-interaction-picture]] clause (e)).

[F3] **Framework and inner-product readings.** $\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}$ are unit vectors and the pairing is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second, with $|\langle u,v\rangle|\le\|u\|\|v\|$ ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]; [[def-inner-product-space]]; [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-for-real-and-complex-inner-product-spaces]]); $W$ self-adjoint bounded means $\langle W\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\rangle=\overline{\langle W\varphi_{j},\varphi_{i}\rangle}$ and $|\langle W\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\rangle|\le\|W\|$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]); the outcome-law reading is that of P2 ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a), (b); [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]; [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]); times and energies are read in seconds and joules as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; instantiate the supplier's amplitude expansion, evaluate the sinusoidal integral by the exponential form of the cosine, and estimate the probability difference by the difference of the amplitudes.

**Given:** the data of the Statement and [F1]-[F3].

1.1 [Exact pair amplitude without completeness] The interaction-picture supplier in [F2] gives $U=E(t)U_IE(-s)$ and $U_I=I+D_1+T_2$ with $D_1\xi=-(i/\hbar)\int_s^tV_I(r)\xi\,dr$ and $\|T_2\|\le e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^2/2$. For the two specified eigenvectors, $\langle E(t)x,\varphi_j\rangle=e^{-iE_jt/\hbar}\langle x,\varphi_j\rangle$ and $E(-s)\varphi_i=e^{iE_is/\hbar}\varphi_i$, so the correct model amplitude is $A_{ji}=e^{i(E_i-E_j)s/\hbar}\langle U_I\varphi_i,\varphi_j\rangle$. Its zeroth term is $\delta_{ij}$. Also $\langle V_I(r)\varphi_i,\varphi_j\rangle=e^{i(E_j-E_i)r/\hbar}\langle V(r)\varphi_i,\varphi_j\rangle$. Passing this continuous bounded linear pairing through the vector integral gives exactly $A^{(1)}_{ji}$ and $R_{ji}=e^{i(E_i-E_j)s/\hbar}\langle T_2\varphi_i,\varphi_j\rangle$, with the advertised remainder by [F3]. Only the fixed pair was used; a complete eigenfamily is unnecessary. For the selected integrable coefficient of $V_0$, subtracting the two first-order scalar integrals and using $|\langle(V-V_0)\varphi_i,\varphi_j\rangle|\le\eta$ proves the stated $\hbar^{-1}\int_s^t\eta$ bound. This proves (a), including free, zero-time and diagonal cases. [F1, F2, F3, given, algebra]

1.2 [Sinusoidal evaluation] With $V(r)=W\cos(\omega r+\vartheta)$ and $u:=r-s$, $\omega r+\vartheta=\omega u+\vartheta_{0}$, so $\cos(\omega r+\vartheta)=\frac{1}{2}(e^{i(\omega u+\vartheta_{0})}+e^{-i(\omega u+\vartheta_{0})})$ and $$A^{(1)}_{ji}=-\frac{i}{2\hbar}\bigl\langle W\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\bigr\rangle\Bigl[e^{i\vartheta_{0}}\int_{0}^{\tau}e^{i(\Delta+\hbar\omega)u/\hbar}du+e^{-i\vartheta_{0}}\int_{0}^{\tau}e^{i(\Delta-\hbar\omega)u/\hbar}du\Bigr],$$ the two integrals being $\tau$ when their frequency vanishes and $(e^{i\theta\tau/\hbar}-1)/(i\theta/\hbar)$ otherwise; this is the displayed decomposition with $a_{\pm}$ and the stated convention. For $a_{+}$, $|e^{i\theta\tau/\hbar}-1|=2|\sin(\theta\tau/(2\hbar))|$ and the modulus of the quotient by $i\theta/\hbar$ is $2\hbar|\sin(\theta\tau/(2\hbar))|/|\theta|$ for $\theta=\Delta-\hbar\omega\ne0$, giving $|a_{+}|=|\langle W\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\rangle||\sin((\Delta-\hbar\omega)\tau/(2\hbar))|/|\Delta-\hbar\omega|$; at $\Delta=\hbar\omega$ the quotient is $\tau$ and the same modulus formula gives the limit $|\langle W\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\rangle|\tau/(2\hbar)$. For $a_{-}$ the same computation gives $|a_{-}|=|\langle W\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\rangle||\sin((\Delta+\hbar\omega)\tau/(2\hbar))|/|\Delta+\hbar\omega|\le|\langle W\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\rangle|/|\Delta+\hbar\omega|$. This is clause (b). [F1, F3, algebra]

2.1 [Probability error for transition and survival] By [F2], $p_{ji}=|A_{ji}|^2$, and step 1.1 gives $A_{ji}=b_{ji}+R$, where $b_{ji}=\delta_{ij}+A^{(1)}$ and $|R|\le\varepsilon$. The identity $|b+R|^2-|b|^2=2\operatorname{Re}(R\overline b)+|R|^2$ therefore gives $|p_{ji}-|b_{ji}|^2|\le2|b_{ji}|\varepsilon+\varepsilon^2$. For $i\ne j$, $b_{ji}=A^{(1)}$, giving the displayed transition bound; for $i=j$, $b_{ii}=1+A^{(1)}$ and $|b_{ii}|\le1+|A^{(1)}|$, giving the displayed survival bound. No diagonal term is dropped. This proves (c). [step 1.1, F2, F3, algebra]

3.1 [Scope] Only the bounded control, the fixed eigenpair, finite times and the choice hypotheses entered; the remainder grows like $e^{K\tau}\tau^{2}$ and no infinite-time limit, density of states, rate or decay was formed, which is clause (d). [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, given] ∎

## Remarks

- **Resonance versus Rabi oscillation.** Clause (b) shows that the first-order co-rotating amplitude grows linearly in $\tau$ at exact resonance. That linear growth is the small-coupling, short-time first-order behaviour of the general bounded-control model; the exact bounded oscillation of the two-level circular drive is proved separately on this page for the declared finite model, and the two statements have different hypotheses: the first applies to any bounded control with an orthonormal eigenpair, the second is exact for the declared two-level family.
- **What "first order" controls.** The bound of clause (a) is uniform in the labels and in the family; it is a bound on the amplitude, not a rate, and the counter-rotating bound of clause (b) shows explicitly how far the physical first-order term is from its co-rotating part.

The theorem is conditional on a bounded self-adjoint control and an orthonormal eigenfamily of H0; it asserts no long-time limit, no Fermi golden rule, no continuum density of states, no transition rate, no decay and no empirical result.

items.title: The common-domain driven model: strong propagator with domain invariance, and the driven oscillator as its declared instance
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the framework data and the declared driven model of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] in the **common-domain class** of clause (b)(iii): $\mathfrak H$ is the model's state space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), $Y\subseteq\mathfrak H$ is a dense linear subspace that is itself a Hilbert space continuously embedded in $\mathfrak H$, $D(H(t))=Y$ for every $t\in I=[a,b]$, every $H(t)$ is self-adjoint as an operator on $\mathfrak H$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), and $t\mapsto H(t)$ is of class $C^{1}(I;\mathcal B(Y,\mathfrak H))$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]); put $L:=\sup_{t\in I}\|H'(t)\|_{\mathcal B(Y,\mathfrak H)}<\infty$ and $A(t):=H(t)/\hbar$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) *Well-posedness of the declared model.* There is a family $U(t,s)$, $a\le s\le t\le b$ on $I$, of unitary operators on $\mathfrak H$ with $U(s,s)=I$, the cocycle $U(t,r)=U(t,s)U(s,r)$, joint strong continuity in $(t,s)$, and:
$$U(t,s)Y=Y,\qquad \|U(t,s)y\|_Y\le C_{I}\|y\|_Y\quad(y\in Y), \qquad i\hbar\,\partial_{t}U(t,s)y=H(t)U(t,s)y\quad(y\in Y),$$
where the derivative is in $\mathfrak H$ and $C_{I}<\infty$ is independent of the endpoints and depends on the actual graph equivalence of $Y$ with $D(H(t)/\hbar)$ as well as $I$ and $L/\hbar$; this family is unique among bounded families with the same strong equation on $Y$, $U(s,s)=I$ and locally bounded strong orbits. The model's clause (c)(iii) declaration therefore has exactly one solution.

(b) *Reverse and adjoint equations.* With $U(s,t):=U(t,s)^{-1}$ one has $U(t,s)^{*}=U(s,t)$ and $i\hbar\partial_{s}U(t,s)y=-U(t,s)H(s)y$ for $y\in Y$; equivalently $i\hbar\partial_{s}U(s,t)y=H(s)U(s,t)y$. The domain maps $(t,s)\mapsto U(t,s)|_{Y}$ are jointly strongly continuous in $\mathcal B(Y)$.

(c) *Declared instance: the driven oscillator.* Let $m,\omega,\hbar>0$ and let $(H_{\mathrm{osc}},Q)$ be the energy and position observables of the one-dimensional oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (b), (c) on $L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx)$, with $Y=D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ carrying the graph norm, and let $f\in C^{1}(I;\mathbb R)$. Declare, as a further model assumption of the pair, the **driven oscillator family**
$$H(t):=H_{\mathrm{osc}}-f(t)Q\qquad(t\in I),$$
read as the system's energy at time $t$, with $f(t)Q$ in joules for $f(t)$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-1}}$. Then for every $t$ the operator $H(t)$ is self-adjoint on the single domain $Y$, the family belongs to $C^{1}(I;\mathcal B(Y,L^{2}))$ with derivative $-f'(t)Q$, and the hypotheses of clause (a) are satisfied with $\mathfrak H=L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx)$; consequently the driven oscillator has a unique strong propagator preserving $D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ and satisfying $i\hbar\partial_{t}U(t,s)y=H(t)U(t,s)y$ for $y\in D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$.

(d) *Scope.* The theorem is conditional on the common-domain regularity class and on the cited oscillator construction; it asserts no existence statement outside that class, no explicit solution, no long-time or adiabatic statement, no measurement and no empirical comparison.

## Facts & Assumptions


**Given:** the declared driven model in the common-domain class with data $Y$, $H(t)$, $L$, $A=H/\hbar$; where clause (c) applies, the oscillator data $m,\omega,\hbar$, $H_{\mathrm{osc}}$, $Q$, and $f\in C^{1}(I;\mathbb R)$; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice.

[F1] **Common-domain supplier.** Under the hypotheses of the Statement with a generator family $A(t)$ of class $C^{1}([0,T];\mathcal B(Y,H))$ and $L=\sup_{t}\|A'(t)\|_{\mathcal B(Y,H)}$, there is a family $U(t,s)$ for $0\le s\le t\le T$ of unitary operators on $H$ with $U(s,s)=I$, the cocycle, joint strong continuity on $\{s\le t\}$ for each $\xi\in H$, $U(t,s)Y=Y$ with $\|U(t,s)y\|_Y\le C_T\|y\|_Y$ for a constant independent of $(s,t)$, and $t\mapsto U(t,s)y$ of class $C^1$ in $H$ with $i\partial_tU(t,s)y=A(t)U(t,s)y$ for $y\in Y$; the family is unique among bounded families with the same strong equation, $U(s,s)=I$ and bounded strong orbits; $U(s,t):=U(t,s)^{-1}$ satisfies $i\partial_sU(s,t)y=A(s)U(s,t)y$ and $U(t,s)^{*}=U(s,t)$, and the domain maps are jointly strongly continuous in $Y$ ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-common-domain-nonautonomous-evolution]] clauses (a)-(c)).

[F2] **Driven-oscillator instance.** For $m,\omega,\hbar>0$, length $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, the oscillator energy $H_{\mathrm{osc}}=\hbar\omega(N_\psi+\frac12I)$ with domain $Y=D(N_\psi)$, position and momentum $Q,P$ of the model, and $f\in C^{1}([a,b];\mathbb R)$: for every $\psi\in Y$ one has $\|Q\psi\|\le\eta\|H_{\mathrm{osc}}\psi\|+b_\eta\|\psi\|$ for every $\eta>0$ (so $Q$ is $H_{\mathrm{osc}}$-bounded with relative bound $0$), for every $t$ the operator $H(t)=H_{\mathrm{osc}}-f(t)Q$ is self-adjoint on the single domain $Y$, and $t\mapsto H(t)$ is of class $C^{1}([a,b];\mathcal B(Y,L^{2}))$ with derivative $-f'(t)Q$ ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-driven-oscillator-common-domain]] clauses (b), (c)).

[F3] **Model readings.** The model declares the class-(iii) family as its energy and clause (c)(iii) as its evolution demand ([[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] clauses (b)(iii), (c)(iii), (d)); the oscillator model supplies the assigned energy observable $(H_{\mathrm{osc}},\mathrm J)$, the position observable $(Q,\mathrm m)$ with unit $\mathrm m$, and the flow generated by $H_{\mathrm{osc}}$ ([[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (b), (c); [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]; [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]; [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; instantiate the common-domain supplier at the model's generator family and check the oscillator family against its hypotheses.

**Given:** the data of the Statement and [F1]-[F3].

1.1 [Well-posedness] The generator family $A(t)=H(t)/\hbar$ has $D(A(t))=Y$ for every $t$, is self-adjoint on $H$ as a scalar multiple of $H(t)$, and belongs to $C^{1}(I;\mathcal B(Y,H))$ with $A'(t)=H'(t)/\hbar$ and $\sup_t\|A'(t)\|_{\mathcal B(Y,H)}=L/\hbar<\infty$; these are exactly the hypotheses of [F1] with $T=b-a$ and the time reparametrisation $t\mapsto t-a$, so [F1] supplies the family $U$ with all displayed properties and identifies it with the model's clause (c)(iii). For explicit dependence, put $K(t)=A(t)-i:Y\to\mathfrak H$, $M=\sup_t\|K(t)^{-1}\|_{\mathfrak H\to Y}$, $N=\sup_t\|K(t)\|_{Y\to\mathfrak H}$, and $L_A=L/\hbar$. The bounded inverse and local Neumann construction in [F1], shows $M,N<\infty$ on compact $I$, without a further hypothesis. Its frozen-product construction bounds the frozen products and limiting evolution in $Y$ by a uniform constant controlled by $MN e^{L_A M(b-a)}$, with the endpoint graph conversions described there. Thus the genuine family-dependent graph constants, rather than $I,L$ alone, control $C_I$. This is clause (a). [F1, F3, given]

2.1 [Reverse and adjoint equations] The second and third assertions of [F1] give $U(t,s)^{*}=U(s,t)$ and $i\hbar\partial_{s}U(t,s)y=-U(t,s)H(s)y$ for $y\in Y$ after multiplying by $\hbar$, together with the joint strong continuity of the domain maps in the graph norm of $Y$. This is clause (b). [step 1.1, F1, given]

2.2 [The driven oscillator is an instance] By [F2], $H(t)=H_{\mathrm{osc}}-f(t)Q$ is self-adjoint on the single domain $Y$ for every $t$ and the family is of class $C^{1}(I;\mathcal B(Y,L^{2}))$ with derivative $-f'(t)Q$; this is precisely the common-domain class hypothesis of the model's clause (b)(iii) with $\mathfrak H=L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx)$ and the declared reading of $H(t)$ as the energy by [F3], and the factor $f(t)Q$ carries the unit $\mathrm{J\,m^{-1}}\cdot\mathrm m=\mathrm J$ by [F3]. Applying clause (a) with $H(t)/\hbar$ gives the unique strong propagator with the strong equation on $D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ and domain invariance. This is clause (c). [step 1.1, F1, F2, F3, given, algebra]

3.1 [Scope] Only the common-domain class, the regularity $C^{1}(Y,H)$ and the oscillator's relative-boundedness structure were used; no explicit solution, no asymptotic, adiabatic or long-time statement, no measurement and no empirical comparison was formed, which is clause (d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, given] ∎

## Remarks

- **Why the common domain matters.** The class-(iii) hypothesis gives what the bounded-control class of the mild theorem does not: invariance of the domain $Y$ and a genuine strong Schroedinger equation on $Y$. The price is the stronger regularity assumption, $C^{1}$ in the graph norm rather than mere strong continuity of a bounded control.
- **The oscillator is not a bounded control.** $Q$ is unbounded, so the driven oscillator is outside the bounded-control class; its admissibility is exactly the relative-bound statement of [F2], and the explicit propagator of the oscillator is a separate result used by the page's example.
